# Marilla Cuthbert

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker and farmer  <sub>[v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009), [v1 c6 P36](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0036), [v1 c14 P18](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0018)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Cuthbert  <sub>[v1 c6 P4](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0004), [v1 c8 P11](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0011)</sub>

## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin woman with angular lines and no soft curves. Her dark hair, which exhibits some gray streaks, is twisted up in a tight knot secured aggressively by two wire hairpins. She possesses a mouth that suggests a hidden sense of humor, though it remains largely undeveloped. As she ages, her hair grows grayer, but she retains a gaunt frame and angular stature, with her face softening in expression over time.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c33 P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015)_

## Personality

Marilla is a woman of narrow experience, rigid conscience, and firm, unsentimental principles who prefers practical duty over imagination. She is neat, precise, and highly disciplined, maintaining an exceptionally clean home and yard. Though initially strict, stern, and undemonstrative, she possesses a deep capacity for love and grows deeply attached to Anne. Over time, her hard exterior mellows, revealing a soft and compassionate heart despite her struggle to express affection openly.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P8](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0008), [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009), [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c5 P21](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0021), [v1 c6 P19](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0019), [v1 c8 P13](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0013), [v1 c8 P17](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0017), [v1 c30 P3](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0003), [v1 c33 P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015), [v1 c38 P46](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0046)_

## Traits

- Rigid conscience  <sub>[v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013)</sub>
- Practical and neat  <sub>[v1 c1 P8](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0008), [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>
- Distrustful of sunshine and frivolity  <sub>[v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>
- Undemonstrative  <sub>[v1 c30 P3](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0003)</sub>
- Fear of being overly indulgent or setting her heart too intensely on human creatures  <sub>[v1 c30 P3](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0003)</sub>

## Abilities

- Housekeeping and home management  <sub>[v1 c1 P8](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0008), [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>
- Cooking and baking  <sub>[v1 c16 P27](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0027)</sub>

## Goals

- To raise Anne properly and teach her right from wrong  <sub>[v1 c6 P31](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0031), [v1 c7 P29](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0029), [v1 c19 P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089)</sub>
- To maintain Green Gables and keep her home together with Anne  <sub>[v1 c38 P12](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0012), [v1 c38 P27](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0027), [v1 c38 P28](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0028)</sub>

## History

Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet life at Green Gables with her brother Matthew. Expecting an orphan boy to help Matthew with farmwork, she was shocked when Matthew brought back an orphan girl, Anne Shirley, due to a mistake in the message passed to Mrs. Spencer. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she felt pity for the girl and relented after seeing the harsh prospect of her being taken by Mrs. Blewett. Deciding to keep Anne, Marilla took on the responsibility of raising and disciplining her, gradually growing fond of the spirited girl despite frequent trials caused by Anne's vivid imagination and mishaps. When Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack following the failure of the Abbey Bank, Marilla was left grieving and faced with failing eyesight that threatened her ability to manage Green Gables. She contemplated selling the homestead until Anne decided to forgo her college scholarship to stay home, teach locally, and manage the farm together, allowing them to keep Green Gables.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009), [v1 c3 P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 c3 P4](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0004), [v1 c5 P21](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0021), [v1 c6 P3](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0003), [v1 c6 P19](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0019), [v1 c6 P31](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0031), [v1 c7 P29](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0029), [v1 c12 P46](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0046), [v1 c37 P9](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0009), [v1 c38 P3](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0003), [v1 c38 P12](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0012), [v1 c38 P27](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0027), [v1 c38 P28](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Her mother was bequeathed an amethyst brooch by a seafaring uncle, which was later passed down to Marilla as her most treasured possession  <sub>[v1 c13 P20](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0020)</sub>
- As a small child, she was deeply hurt when an aunt called her a 'dark, homely little thing'  <sub>[v1 c9 P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044)</sub>
- Lived an easy and quiet life at Green Gables prior to adopting Anne  <sub>[v1 c7 P29](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0029)</sub>

## Quotes

> Good evening, Rachel. This is a real fine evening, isn’t it? Won’t you sit down? How are all your folks?  <sub>[v1 c1 P11](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0011)</sub>

> No; you’ll call me just plain Marilla. I’m not used to being called Miss Cuthbert and it would make me nervous.  <sub>[v1 c8 P9](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0009)</sub>

> I’m not your aunt and I don’t believe in calling people names that don’t belong to them.  <sub>[v1 c8 P13](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0013)</sub>

> You shouldn’t have twitted her about her looks, Rachel.  <sub>[v1 c9 P26](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0026)</sub>

> You blessed girl! I feel as if you’d given me new life. I guess I ought to stick out and make you go to college—but I know I can’t, so I ain’t going to try. I’ll make it up to you though, Anne.  <sub>[v1 c38 P28](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0028)</sub>
